title: Make room for one focused session
summary: A visible work timer and an optional focus profile offer two ways to give the next task your attention.
body:
For a simple starting point, Pomodoro puts the remaining time in the Omarchy bar. Its documentation describes both a single countdown and a work-and-break cycle, with a local log of completed work sessions. Choose a duration and start one task.

If the interruption itself is the problem, Focus Modes groups desktop actions into named profiles. Its documented options include do-not-disturb, keeping the screen awake, and moving selected apps out of the way. It also has its own timer, so a separate Pomodoro timer is optional.

Start with the actions you need. Focus Modes' optional website blocking requires a separately installed privileged helper; the author's setup and removal instructions explain that boundary. Radar does not install or configure either plugin. These are two documented approaches to compare, not a claim that the combination has been integration-tested.
